schema_description: Ground truth for the toy 'python_app' fixture (see ../python_app/).
Top-level fields:
fixture_root      : path (relative to this file's ../..) of the source tree the claims are about.
claims            : list of ClaimGroundTruth objects, described below.
ClaimGroundTruth fields (kept close to the ArchitecturalClaim / EvidenceItem
vocabulary used elsewhere in this initiative -- claim_id/text/epistemic_type/
support_status/evidence -- so a future wiring-up to the real domain model is a
rename, not a redesign):
claim_id                : short stable id, referenced by candidate claim sets.
text                    : natural-language claim text.
category                : one of the 4 evaluation buckets --
'supported_observed'    - true, single evidence item suffices.
'supported_multi_hop'    - true, requires chaining >=2 evidence items.
'insufficient_evidence'  - plausible-sounding but the fixture neither
confirms nor denies it (no evidence exists
either way). This includes claims about a
behavior/relationship the analyzer simply
cannot find any code for -- absence of a
match is NOT treated as a refutation (see
claims C6/C7/C8/C9).
'contradicted'            - false, and the available evidence positively
establishes an INCOMPATIBLE fact -- not just an
absence of confirming evidence. Reserved for
claims about a closed, authoritative structural
relation (e.g. an explicit class-inheritance
declaration, whose direct base-class list is
complete by construction) where the actual fact
is provably incompatible with the claim (see C10).
expected_support_status : the ClaimSupportStatus a correct system should output --
'supported' | 'insufficient_evidence' | 'contradicted'.
(For category supported_observed/supported_multi_hop this is always
'supported'; for insufficient_evidence/contradicted categories this
equals the category name -- the category IS the expected status.)
expected_epistemic_type : the ClaimEpistemicType a correct system should output --
'observed' (directly evidenced by one fact) |
'inferred' (requires chaining/combining evidence).
expected_evidence       : ordered list of EvidenceItemGroundTruth (empty list for
insufficient_evidence claims, since no evidence exists either way).
Order matters for multi-hop claims: it is the hop order of the chain.
EvidenceItemGroundTruth fields:
evidence_id       : short stable id local to this claim.
evidence_type     : 'source_span' | 'relationship'.
hop_index          : 1-based position in the evidence chain (null for single-hop claims).
file               : path relative to fixtures/ (e.g. 'python_app/controllers/order_controller.py').
start_line/end_line: 1-based inclusive line range in `file` that constitutes the evidence.
symbol_id           : dotted id of the enclosing symbol, for evidence_type='source_span'.
relationship_type   : 'calls' | 'operates_on' | 'inherits', for evidence_type='relationship'.
source_symbol_id    : dotted id of the relationship's source symbol, for evidence_type='relationship'.
target_symbol_id    : dotted id of the relationship's target symbol, for evidence_type='relationship'.
supports_or_refutes : 'supports' | 'refutes'. Almost all evidence items support their claim;
for 'contradicted' claims the cited evidence instead REFUTES the claim
(e.g. OrderRepository's actual, complete base-class list, which a correct
system should cite as the reason claim C10 -- asserting a different base
class -- is false).
note               : free-text explanation of why this evidence item is relevant.
Symbol id convention: '<dotted module path>.<ClassName>.<method_name>' or
'<dotted module path>.<ClassName>' for a class as a whole, rooted at 'python_app'.

claims.text: OrderService.create_order calls PaymentService.charge to process payment.
OrderService.create_order calls OrderRepository.save to persist the order.
OrderController transitively depends on the Order entity, via OrderService and OrderRepository.

expected_evidence.note: Hop 3: Repository.save operates on the Order entity ('self._orders[order.order_id] = order').

claims.text: OrderController transitively depends on PaymentService for payment processing, via OrderService.
OrderController requires the customer to be authenticated via OAuth2 before placing an order.
claims.note: Nothing in the fixture implements or references authentication of any kind, so this is neither confirmed nor denied -- it is simply unaddressed.

claims.text: OrderService sends a confirmation email to the customer after placing an order.
claims.note: create_order() only charges and persists; there is no email/notification code anywhere in the fixture, but also no code that positively rules email out -- unaddressed, not refuted.

claims.text: PaymentService.charge performs fraud detection (risk scoring / anomaly analysis) on transactions before charging them.
claims.note: CORRECTED (2026-08-07): previously misclassified as 'contradicted' on the theory that the full visible body of charge() containing no fraud-detection code refutes the claim. That is an absence-of-evidence argument, not a positive incompatible fact -- the analyzed representation only shows what THIS method does, not that fraud detection cannot happen anywhere else (e.g. in a real gateway this mock stands in for, or upstream middleware). Per corrected support-status semantics, absence of a matching relationship/behavior must be insufficient_evidence, never contradicted. See claim C10 for a genuine contradiction built on a closed, authoritative fact instead.

claims.text: OrderRepository persists Order entities to a SQL database.
claims.note: CORRECTED (2026-08-07): previously misclassified as 'contradicted' on the theory that the visible in-memory dict storage in this file, with no SQL/ORM/DB client referenced, refutes the claim. That is the same absence-of-evidence flaw as the former C8: not finding SQL usage in one file does not positively establish SQL is never used anywhere in the system. Per corrected support-status semantics this must be insufficient_evidence. See claim C10 for a genuine contradiction built on a closed, authoritative fact (explicit class inheritance) instead.

expected_evidence.note: 'class OrderRepository(InMemoryRepository):' -- a class statement's direct base-class list is complete and AST-visible by construction (unlike runtime behavior, which can never be fully enumerated by reading one file). The actual, complete base list is exactly {InMemoryRepository}; SqlRepository is not, and cannot be, an undeclared additional direct base. This positively establishes a fact (the true base) incompatible with the claim, which is what makes this a genuine CONTRADICTED case rather than an insufficient_evidence one -- contrast with C8/C9.
